prompt: On January 13, 1979, a 15-cent stamp honoring Martin Luther King, Jr. was issued by the United States Postal Service as part of the Black Heritage Series of commemorative stamps. In 1979, it cost 15¢ to mail a first class letter weighing up to 1 ounce, and the current cost to mail a first class letter weighing no more than 1 ounce is 78¢. Suppose \$24,965,253 worth of the Black Heritage King stamps have been issued by the USPS. Using only those 15-cent commemorative King stamps that have been issued, how many first class letters weighing up to 1 ounce each could be mailed today?

solutions.title: Stamps per letter
solutions.body:
A letter needs at least 78¢, and 15-cent stamps give 75¢ (too little) with 5 stamps, so 6 stamps = 90¢ are needed per letter. Letters: $\$24{,}965{,}253 \div \$0.90 = 27{,}739{,}170$.

**Answer: 27,739,170 letters**

What is the total amount of money that would be saved by instead using a combination of commemorative 15-cent King stamps, 10-cent stamps and 1-cent stamps to mail the same number of first class letters weighing up to 1 ounce each?

On January 13, 1979, a 15-cent stamp honoring Martin Luther King, Jr. was issued by the United States Postal Service as part of the Black Heritage Series of commemorative stamps. In 1979, it cost 15¢ to mail a first class letter weighing up to 1 ounce, and the current cost to mail a first class letter weighing no more than 1 ounce is 78¢. Suppose \$24,965,253 worth of the Black Heritage King stamps have been issued by the USPS. What is the percent decrease in the total number of first class letters that can be mailed using \$24,965,253 worth of first class postage today compared to 1979, when the commemorative King stamp was first issued? Express your answer as a percent to the nearest tenth.

solutions.title: Use the price ratio
solutions.body:
The number of letters is the money divided by the price, so today's count is $\frac{15}{78}$ of 1979's count. Percent decrease $= 1 - \frac{15}{78} = \frac{63}{78} \approx 0.8077 = 80.8\%$.

**Answer: 80.8%**
